When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10** (WATCH, almost no stress signals firing in price action) vs VIX Spike Tier **4/4** EXTREME (**85%** probability, skew and backwardation and adaptive all active)
Realized price stress is near zero while the options market prices an extreme vol expansion. Trust the VIX Spike read: backwardation means near-dated implied vol is trading above longer-dated vol, a structure that precedes sharp moves rather than drifts. The Crash Index is backward-looking on realized price; the VIX Spike Detector reads forward-implied fear. When they split like this, the options market is early. It is rarely wrong.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **43/100** (ACCUMULATE, partial buy signal) vs Divergence composite TOPPING zone (**74.4%** of pairs diverging, **28** bearish vs **4** bullish)
The contrarian model says conditions are beginning to favor mean-reversion longs, but the cross-asset divergence picture shows the market's internal structure breaking down at scale. Trust the divergence read: **43/100** is only a partial signal, and **28** bearish diverging pairs against **4** bullish is too wide a gap to buy into with conviction.
Today's tension
The options market is pricing an extreme vol event while spot equity price action shows almost no stress.
Bull
NDX is up **5.3%** on the week and BTC is up **4.3%**, confirming that risk appetite in growth and crypto remains alive. The Contrarian score at **43/100** is a partial ACCUMULATE signal, which argues against pressing short bets aggressively.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector is at Tier **4/4** EXTREME with **85%** probability, and skew, backwardation, and adaptive triggers are all active at once. **74.4%** of cross-asset pairs are diverging in the TOPPING zone, with **28** bearish pairs against only **4** bullish ones.
The tell: VIX term-structure backwardation: if near-term implied vol reverts below longer-dated vol (contango), the fear premium unwinds and the TRANSITION regime can resolve to the upside. If backwardation holds, the options market wins.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime is in TRANSITION at 43/100 with a MIXED bias, and the macro regime is CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence. Together they describe a market where index-level clarity is low but the internal story is sharp. NDX is up 5.3% over five days while DJI is down 1.1%, and 74.4% of cross-asset pairs are diverging in the TOPPING zone with 28 bearish pairs against 4 bullish. The headline indices are masking what is happening. The internals are the signal.

For positioning, TRANSITION plus CONCENTRATION means sizing down gross index exposure and staying close to the names driving NDX leadership. The Contrarian score at 43/100 (partial ACCUMULATE) argues against pressing shorts: conditions are beginning to tilt toward mean reversion. You stay long the concentration trade and short the cyclical laggards. DJI at -1.1% versus NDX at +5.3% is a pair trade the regime is endorsing directly.

The main risk is the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 with 85% probability and all three sub-signals active. That is forward-looking fear, priced in the options market before it shows up in price. The reading that flips the entire stance is VIX backwardation collapsing back to contango: near-dated vol reverting below longer-dated vol signals the hedging demand is fading and the TRANSITION regime can resolve bullishly. Until then, treat the options market as the lead signal.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence, in plain terms, means two assets or indicators that normally move together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift means the historical co-movement between two things has shifted in direction or magnitude.

The divergence composite is in the TOPPING zone: 74.4% of the 43 tracked pairs are diverging, with 28 showing bearish divergence and only 4 showing bullish. The Mother Jaws score is at 100, a full-alarm reading.

Among the six deepest-diverging pairs, QQQ and SPY have drifted from +0.79 correlation to -0.34: mega-cap tech is decoupling from the broader equity market. USMV (a low-volatility equity fund) has flipped from -0.92 to +0.09 correlation with SPY, meaning the usual defensive rotation pattern has broken down.

KRE and XLF (regional banks vs. broad financials) have drifted from +0.18 to -0.62.

When this many relationships fracture simultaneously in the TOPPING zone, the market's internal structure is breaking down even as the headline index holds.

AI read · the cross-region tape

The five-day global tape tells a consistent story: growth-oriented markets lead, cyclical or broad markets lag. The KOSPI is the strongest index across all regions at +4.8% while the ASX sits at -0.2%, a stark gap within Asia.

In Europe, the STOXX 50 at +0.9% leads the CAC at +0.3%, a narrower spread but the same direction. In the US, NDX at +5.3% versus DJI at -1.1% is the sharpest divergence of the week.

BTC at +4.3% and SOL at +2.1% add crypto confirmation to the risk-on read in speculative assets. The implication for today's US session: the growth-tech bid has global support, but the DJI is telling you the rally has not broadened into cyclicals.

Adding broad US equity exposure here means buying a narrow bet.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 EXTREME are reading two different markets at two different time horizons. The gap between them is coherent.

The Crash Index measures current equity price-regime stress: at 1, almost no signals are firing in realized price action. The VIX Spike Detector reads the options market's forward-looking fear: at Tier 4/4 with 85% probability, near-term implied vol is trading above longer-dated vol (backwardation), and skew and adaptive triggers are both active.

You have calm spot prices and a fearful options market simultaneously. That is a pre-event structure.

The options market is paying up for protection the equity tape has not yet required. When this gap closes, it almost always closes because spot volatility rises to meet implied, not the other way around.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
